caller_tactics.text: Hello, is this Eszter? I'm Leon Brandt, from Westmere Federal Savings. You asked about government savings bonds at the branch last week.
Of course. Savings bonds are issued by the government, and they pay a fixed rate for a set term. You can buy them through our branch.
The rate is published on the government's website and updated each month. I'd check there for the figure that applies to you.
You can, but if you cash it before it's been held for a year, you don't earn interest for the last three months. The rules are on the official page.
There is an annual purchase limit per person, which is set by the government. I'll give you the exact amount in the printed information.
No, they are not linked to the stock market. The return is set when you buy, and the value doesn't move with shares.
Not at all. You're welcome to take the information away and read it when you like.
Yes, I'll put it in the post this afternoon. There's also a short explainer on the government site that's quite clear.
You're welcome, Eszter. Call the branch whenever you have questions.
